title: Ant OceanBase Launches AI Data Platform: Unifies Multimodal Data Management and Provides Business Context for Agents

content_html:
On November 24, the OceanBase AI Data Conference was held in Beijing. At the conference, OceanBase CEO Yang Bing said that as models become increasingly advanced and Agent infrastructure becomes increasingly mature, the challenge will ultimately return to data. In response to this shift, data infrastructure in the AI era should adhere to four principles: "integrated data lake and database, multimodal fusion, Agent-friendly, and open-source and open." Guided by this direction, OceanBase officially launched its strategic AI product—OceanLake, an AI data platform with integrated data lake and database capabilities—and announced that it would open-source its core engine, the AI database, to the world, inviting developers and industry partners to jointly build data infrastructure for AI.

Yang Bing believes that the intelligent transformation of enterprises today is far below expectations. First, the commoditization of model capabilities has already been completed: capabilities are improving rapidly and costs continue to decline, so the models themselves are no longer the bottleneck. Second, the "low-hanging fruit" has been picked clean; the value of public data has been largely exhausted. Third, a new business flywheel has not yet formed; the mutual reinforcement and co-evolution of business and data has not yet been realized.

He further summarized the difficulties in unlocking enterprise data productivity as "three icebergs": the first lies between private data and public data—without mining the value of private data, productivity cannot truly be unleashed; the second lies between multimodal data and structured data—multimodal data will bring more incremental value; the third lies between messy data and orderly data—organizing messy data is a necessary condition for unlocking data productivity.
